Divs are fixed rectangles that act like mini canvases. 
You could technachly do anything by using just divs 
and passing the appropiate parameters.
+------------------------------------------------+ 
|    col1 |                                 col2 |
|         |                 _______              |
|_________|                |   div |             |
|     div |                |_______|             |
|         |                                      |
|         |                                      |
+------------------------------------------------+ 
Columns allow you to split up space horizontally according
to specific ratios like [0.3, 0.7] for example.

#### fuse_div_begin_scroll {#fuse_div_begin_scroll}

Source: `Fuse.h:337`

```c
void fuse_div_begin_scroll(FuseCanvas, float x, float y, float w, float h, const FuseClass *cls, float *scroll);
```

#### fuse_div_scope {#fuse_div_scope}

Source: `Fuse.h:343`

```c
void fuse_div_scope(FuseCanvas);
```

After opening a stable named div, scope explicitly named child IDs to its ID.
Call before child IDs/queries. Ordinary nested divs inherit; a nested scope
combines its own scoped ID with child names. div_end restores the outer scope.
No scope means names remain canvas-global (legacy behavior). Anonymous child
IDs already derive from parent IDs. Requires an open div; no extra storage.

#### fuse_scope_enter {#fuse_scope_enter}

Source: `Fuse.h:349`

```c
uint32_t fuse_scope_enter(FuseCanvas, const char *name);
```

Temporarily enter a named child scope without emitting a layout element.
Resolves name against the current scope, exactly like id + div_scope.
Pair with restore(previous) in LIFO order before closing enclosing divs or
building other panels. Tokens are canvas-local; clear resets this override.
Intended for focus/edit queries outside panel building; no allocation.

#### fuse_scope_restore {#fuse_scope_restore}

Source: `Fuse.h:350`

```c
void fuse_scope_restore(FuseCanvas, uint32_t previous);
```

#### fuse_div_end {#fuse_div_end}

#### fuse_window_begin {#fuse_window_begin}

Source: `Fuse.h:379`

```c
void fuse_window_begin(FuseCanvas, char *name, float x, float y, float w, float h, const FuseClass *cls);
```

Windows / docking is a necessary feature of modern editing software.
Maybe in a 2.0 version of Fuse, I could find a way to merge divs
and windows, but I don't find that necessary or an issue.

CANVAS
+-----------------------+------------------------+ 
|  _______           DIV|            |    DOCKING|
| |   _[]X|     _______ |            |           |
| |       |    |   _[]X||           <|>          |
| |       |    |       ||           <|>          |
| |_______|    |       ||            |           |    
|              |_______||win1        |win2       |                
+------------------------------------------------+ 

Windows act similar to divs in the sense that they also act as 
containers for the elements drawn inside of them.

A docking div would allow you to customize how you want windows to
be docked / tiled. Otherwise, windows will act in a "floating" manner
similar to what is seen in non-tiling desktop environments like Windows.
Standalone named div wrappers; persistent docking API is below.

Stems the next element. Replaces the parent class on that axis.

#### fuse_textbox {#fuse_textbox}

Source: `Fuse.h:416`

```c
bool fuse_textbox(FuseCanvas, float x, float y, float w, float h, float pad_l, float pad_r,
    char *buf, int cap, int *caret, const char *placeholder, float size,
    uint32_t fill, uint32_t hovered, uint32_t ink, uint32_t ghost, int caret_on,
    int (*allow)(unsigned char ch, void *user), void *user);
```

One-line field. Call fuse_id first. buf is NUL-terminated, cap includes the NUL.
pad_l and pad_r inset the glyphs. placeholder is drawn when buf is empty.
caret_on shows the caret while the box is focused. allow may be NULL,
which keeps bytes 32..126. Returns 1 when buf changes.

#### fuse_textbox_edit {#fuse_textbox_edit}

Source: `Fuse.h:423`

```c
bool fuse_textbox_edit(FuseCanvas, const char *name, char *buf, int cap, int *caret,
    int (*allow)(unsigned char ch, void *user), void *user);
```

Applies the queued edit to buf when name is the focused field.
Use this before layout that depends on the text. The later text box
call draws that result and does not apply the same keys again.

#### fuse_radial_pick {#fuse_radial_pick}

Source: `Fuse.h:443`

```c
int fuse_radial_pick(float cx, float cy, float inner, float outer, int count, float px, float py);
```

Annular menu, 1..8 slices. Slice 0 is centered to the right; indices
increase clockwise in screen coordinates. Inner/outer boundaries cancel;
angular boundaries belong to the following slice. Invalid/nonfinite input
returns -1. Pointer coordinates are relative to the same parent as center.
The caller owns capture, release, labels and actions. No input is consumed.
Drawing uses at most 144 triangle commands; no heap allocation. Link libm.
Rebuild consumers and size canvas buffers with fuse_canvas_memory:
FuseCmd grew by one float. The menu is a fixed-size drawing leaf.

#### fuse_radial {#fuse_radial}

Source: `Fuse.h:444`

```c
int fuse_radial(FuseCanvas, float cx, float cy, float inner, float outer, int count,
    float px, float py, uint32_t idle, uint32_t hovered);
```

Image in the layout, same coordinates as fuse_rect. w and h are the
displayed size (intrinsic pixels times the caller's scale).

#### fuse_text {#fuse_text}

Text, font and bitmaps.
Built-in 5x7 bitmap, the fallback face. One layout element per string;
glyph runs are its children, each glyph pixel s by s. s snaps to an integer.

#### PeakIOCode {#peakiocode}

Source: `Peak.h:511`

```c
typedef enum {
    PEAK_IO_OK, PEAK_IO_INVALID, PEAK_IO_LIMIT,
    PEAK_IO_NOT_REGULAR, PEAK_IO_UNSUPPORTED, PEAK_IO_SYSTEM
} PeakIOCode;
```

Safe I/O (independent of peak_init): Linux openat2 only; other hosts and
kernels lacking the required resolution flags return PEAK_IO_UNSUPPORTED.
No fallback to ordinary path-based I/O. Native Windows/macOS qualification
is pending. Legacy peak_file_* / peak_filesystem_* retain their semantics.

Ownership: initialize caller storage with *_INIT before first use. Successful
opens/begin fill an empty output; failures leave it empty. These are owning,
non-copyable values, not borrowed descriptors. Do not edit their fields,
close their native handles yourself, or use them concurrently with close.
Close consumes a handle even on error; commit/abort consume both stage
handles on every outcome for a live stage. Separate objects may be used
concurrently; operations on a stage must be externally serialized.

Paths: root_open takes an absolute path ("/" is allowed); all *_at/open/begin
paths are nonempty normalized relative paths. No empty, dot, dot-dot, or
symlink components, trailing slash, or absolute relative paths are allowed.
Limits: 4095 path bytes, 255 bytes/component, 128 components, byte limits
representable as a native nonnegative file offset. No heap allocations.
Every relative lookup is kernel-resolved beneath its owning directory
handle with RESOLVE_BENEATH | RESOLVE_NO_SYMLINKS | RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS.
Mount points/hard links are not rejected: these are not authorization,
provenance, or immutable-snapshot primitives. Files are verified regular.

Handles pin directory/file objects, not pathnames. Root or parent rename/
replacement does not redirect an existing handle. A retained directory may
be moved outside the original tree; later operations still target that
object, not the current object at its former path. Reads are bounded but
not snapshots: uncooperative in-place writers can change bytes/size during
a read. size is only the initial observed file size; hash/validation policy
and coordination with writers belong to the caller.

Staging: destination's parent MUST be cooperatively/exclusively controlled
against uncooperative directory writers (including same-user writers).
A named stage is not safe against such writers swapping/unlinking its name
between creation, rename, and cleanup. temporary_leaf is caller-selected,
single-component and distinct from destination's leaf; O_EXCL never reuses
an existing entry. Use an appropriately unpredictable/reserved name and
authorize/serialize the destination yourself. The stage is visible by its
temporary name (mode 0600), so callers must exclude stages from asset lookup.
Commit atomically replaces a non-directory destination entry via renameat;
it does not follow a destination symlink. No no-clobber/version checks,
metadata preservation, backups, or multi-file/bundle transaction policy.
Previous-file preservation on failure applies only within the cooperative
contract; external races are not covered. All stages are same-parent.

Bounded read is positional, reports partial progress on failure and EOF via
read_bytes < bytes. It rejects a currently observed size above limit, but
cannot detect every transient growth or mutation. Stage writes are sequential
and bounded in aggregate; any invalid/failed write poisons publication.
Successful commit without durability only establishes publication. With
FILE_AND_DIRECTORY, fsync(stage) precedes rename and fsync(parent) follows;
durable=1 means both succeeded, subject to filesystem/hardware guarantees;
durable=0 means durability was not established, not that bytes were lost.
This does not fsync ancestor directories or establish durability of newly
created directory hierarchies. Byte bounds are not elapsed-time deadlines.
A post-rename error NEVER means unpublished: inspect published separately.
published is 0 (not attempted/not published), 1 (rename succeeded), or -1
(rename failed ambiguously; e.g. a lost remote FS reply). Destination type/
nonempty-directory errors are definite failures within the cooperative
contract; other rename errors are conservatively reported as uncertain.
Do not interpret -1 as false or true; recovery must inspect/coordinate the
destination. On uncertain publication the temporary name is not removed.
Cleanup reports unlink/close failures independently; a failed pre-publication
cleanup may leave the temporary name for caller-managed recovery. No rollback
after publication. Cleanup success does not establish crash-durable removal
of a temporary name. Invalid finish arguments leave the stage untouched.

#### PeakMemoryDomain {#peakmemorydomain}

Source: `Peak.h:766`

```c
typedef enum {
	PEAK_MEMORY_NON_DRIVER = 0,
	PEAK_MEMORY_DRIVER,
	PEAK_MEMORY_DOMAIN_COUNT
} PeakMemoryDomain;
```

Direct instrumented backing calls only, not libc/DSO or Vulkan internals.
Single-threaded diagnostics; counters persist for the process lifetime.
Each domain has independent fixed live-pointer capacity (512 by default).
Exhaustion leaves request counters valid, but live/release evidence incomplete;
live_blocks/live_bytes/peak_bytes are not exact when tracking is incomplete.
Unknown-pointer operations invalidate BOTH domains' accounting: original
ownership is unknowable. Request counts remain useful but uncertified.
Overflow saturates counters and clears accounting_complete. No reset API.
PEAK_DEBUG_MEMORY_TRACE (default 0) enables per-request output.

#### PeakMemoryStats {#peakmemorystats}

Source: `Peak.h:772`

```c
typedef struct {
	uint64_t allocation_requests; /* successful malloc/calloc/nonzero realloc */
	uint64_t failed_requests;
	uint64_t realloc_requests; /* includes NULL, failure and zero-size release */
	uint64_t released_blocks;
	uint64_t live_blocks;
	uint64_t live_bytes;
	uint64_t peak_bytes; /* requested live bytes, not allocator resident bytes */
	uint64_t domain_errors;
	uint64_t unknown_operations;
	int tracking_complete;
	int accounting_complete;
} PeakMemoryStats;
```

#### peak_clip_set {#peak_clip_set}

Source: `Peak.h:685`

```c
PEAK int peak_clip_set(PeakCtx *ctx, PeakWindow *win, PeakClip which, const char *utf8, size_t n);
```

█  █
█
███ █  █ ███
█   █  █ █ █
█   █  █ █ █
███ ██ █ ███
█
█
Window-only methods validate their owned context. Linux additionally validates
native allocation/slot lifetimes, rejecting copied handles after close/reuse.
Other legacy hosts require exclusive window-handle ownership: do not retain
copies after close or quit; stale-copy validation is not provided there.
UTF-8 clipboard. Configured clipboard cap. win NULL: context-local slot. PRIMARY aliases
CLIPBOARD on Win32/macOS/web. request completes as PEAK_EVENT_CLIP; take copies.

```c
PEAK PeakMemoryStats peak_debug_memory_stats(PeakMemoryDomain domain);
```

#### peak_debug_memory_report {#peak_debug_memory_report}

Source: `Peak.h:797`

```c
PEAK uint64_t peak_debug_memory_report(void);
```

Prints both domains and leaks; returns successful NON_DRIVER requests.
realloc(NULL,0) returns NULL without a backing request or release; every
realloc wrapper call increments realloc_requests, including zero-size calls.
Original tracked domain is authoritative on free/realloc despite mismatch.
Unknown-pointer operations clear completeness; no release is invented.

<!-- END GENERATED API -->

#### RendMemory {#rendmemory-1}

Source: `Rend.h:123`

```c
struct RendMemory {
    void *host_mapped_memory; // pointer if memory is host visible
    uint64_t device_memory; // original device memory pointer
    uint64_t size; // size of the memory allocation AFTER THE OFFSET
    uint64_t offset; // we must sum the offset to device memory
    uint32_t heap_index; // heap index where the memory is located
    uint32_t id; // used by custom allocators
};
```

Unchanged legacy value layouts, needed by the public by-value API.
Renderer/pipeline handles and dispatch records remain implementation-only.

#### RendBuffer {#rendbuffer-1}

Source: `Rend.h:132`

```c
struct RendBuffer {
    RendMemory memory;
    void *mapped_memory; // pointer to offset memory
    void *allocator;
    void *logical_device;
    uint64_t handle;
    uint64_t gpu_address; // addresses must be buffer specific and cannot be generalized into memory because of how vulkan works
    uint32_t usage;
    uint32_t size;
    uint8_t backend;
};
```

```c
};
```

Resume the acquired default color after a completed pass/blit in this frame.
Inside a frame, outside a pass. Loads color, clears depth, transitions the
color target from transfer destination when needed. End with render_end.
Never loads a previous frame or a target from a failed acquire.

```c
typedef enum {
	TYPE_OK = 0,
	TYPE_ERR_INVALID_FONT,
	TYPE_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TABLE,
	TYPE_ERR_GLYPH_NOT_FOUND,
	TYPE_ERR_ATLAS_FULL,
```

#### TypeScratch {#typescratch}

Source: `Type.h:110`

```c
typedef struct TypeScratch {
	uint8_t *data;
	size_t capacity, used, peak;
	int failed;
} TypeScratch;
```

Caller-owned temporary-arena view. No allocation or heap fallback.
Initialize once per borrowed slice. Operations restore used, retain peak and
failed diagnostics. Do not share a view across concurrent/reentrant calls.
data must not overlap context, font bytes, output or bitmap storage.

#### TypeAntiAlias {#typeantialias}

Source: `Type.h:120`

```c
typedef enum {
	TYPE_AA_NONE = 0, /* binary coverage */
	TYPE_AA_BOX = 1,  /* box-filter antialiasing */
	TYPE_AA_SDF = 2,  /* signed distance; raster returns TYPE_ERR_UNIMPLEMENTED */
} TypeAntiAlias;
```

#### TypeWeight {#typeweight}

Source: `Type.h:127`

```c
typedef enum {
	TYPE_WEIGHT_THIN = 100,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_EXTRA_LIGHT = 200,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_LIGHT = 300,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_REGULAR = 400,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_MEDIUM = 500,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_SEMI_BOLD = 600,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_BOLD = 700,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_EXTRA_BOLD = 800,
	TYPE_WEIGHT_BLACK = 900,
} TypeWeight;
```

CSS-ish usWeightClass. Any u16 is legal; these are the named stops.

#### TypeWidth {#typewidth}

Source: `Type.h:140`

```c
typedef enum {

	TYPE_WIDTH_WIDE,
	TYPE_WIDTH_AMBIGUOUS,
	TYPE_WIDTH_NEUTRAL,

```

UAX #11. Neutral is the default outside the wide and ambiguous ranges.

#### TypeParams {#typeparams}

Source: `Type.h:164`

```c
typedef struct TypeParams {
	uint32_t atlas_width;
	uint32_t atlas_height;
	uint32_t cache_capacity;
	uint32_t max_faces;
	uint32_t max_fallbacks;
	uint8_t ligatures;
	uint8_t color_emoji;
	uint8_t antialias;
} TypeParams;
```

atlas_* and cache_capacity must be > 0 (type_params_default fills the
velocitty defaults). max_faces and max_fallbacks bound storage inside the
context buffer. ligatures/color_emoji are reserved; the unshaped helper
applies neither GSUB nor color glyphs. antialias is TypeAntiAlias.


#### TypeBitmap {#typebitmap}

Source: `Type.h:185`

```c
typedef struct TypeBitmap {
	uint16_t width;
	uint16_t height;
	int16_t bearing_x;
	int16_t bearing_y;
	uint16_t advance;
	uint8_t *pixels;
	uint8_t color;
} TypeBitmap;
```

pixels is coverage (1 byte) or straight RGBA8 (4 bytes) when color != 0.
advance is pixels at the requested size. Bearing is the bitmap origin
relative to the pen, y up.

#### TypeGlyph {#typeglyph}

Source: `Type.h:195`

```c
typedef struct TypeGlyph {

	uint16_t glyph_id;

	float bearing_x;
	float bearing_y;
	uint16_t width;
	uint16_t height;
```

#### TypeShapedGlyph {#typeshapedglyph}

Source: `Type.h:220`

```c
typedef struct TypeShapedGlyph {
	uint32_t font_id, glyph_id, cluster;
	float x_advance, y_advance, x_offset, y_offset;
} TypeShapedGlyph;
```

External shaper output, in visual glyph order. cluster is a UTF-8 byte
offset in the caller's logical text, never a glyph index. Positions are
pixels, fractional, y down (negate HarfBuzz y values on import). font_id
and glyph_id must refer to exactly the face shaped, including glyph 0.
Run size uses the same integer-pixel rounding as type_glyph.

#### TypePositionedGlyph {#typepositionedglyph}

```c
typedef struct TypePositionedGlyph {
	TypeGlyph glyph;
	uint32_t cluster;
	float x, y;
} TypePositionedGlyph;
```

#### TypeTextMetrics {#typetextmetrics}

```c
typedef struct TypeTextMetrics {
	float advance_x, advance_y;
	float min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y;
	uint8_t has_ink;
} TypeTextMetrics;
```

Ink bounds relative to initial baseline; advance includes invisible glyphs.
has_ink == 0 means all bounds are zero.

#### type_ttf_place_index {#type_ttf_place_index}

Source: `Type.h:274`

```c
TypeTTF *type_ttf_place_index(void *buf, size_t bufsize, const void *bytes, size_t len,
			      uint32_t face_index);
```

All admission paths validate bounded table views. Nested outlines are checked
on access and may return TYPE_ERR_INVALID_FONT, TYPE_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TABLE or
TYPE_ERR_LIMIT. Font bytes must remain immutable. Placement is 16-byte aligned.
The trusted suffix is retained as an alias, without bypassing validation.
Both placement types accept glyf/CFF/CFF2. TTC chooses face zero by default.

#### type_bitmap_bytes {#type_bitmap_bytes}

Source: `Type.h:332`

```c
size_t type_bitmap_bytes(const TypeBitmap *info);
```

width*height, or *4 when color

#### type_font_render_bitmap {#type_font_render_bitmap}

Source: `Type.h:339`

```c
TypeError type_font_render_bitmap(const TypeFont *font, uint16_t glyph_id, float size_px,
				  TypeAntiAlias aa, void *pixels, size_t len, TypeBitmap *out);
```

pixels must hold type_bitmap_bytes of the info at this size. Empty glyphs
(width or height 0) succeed and leave pixels untouched. On raster scratch
exhaustion coverage is zeroed and out is not published.
Legacy entry point needs no scratch for empty glyphs; otherwise returns
TYPE_ERR_SCRATCH_REQUIRED. Use the explicit-scratch variant for rendering.

#### type_memory {#type_memory}

Source: `Type.h:388`

```c
size_t type_memory(const TypeParams *params);
```

Context reserves memory for all our needs,
based on the parameters we pass to it.

NOTE(vasco): First added face becomes primary. A bold+italic face is remembered
as bold-italic; a bold face as bold; an italic face as italic. Later adds
of the same kind replace that slot. Fallback order is the set_fallbacks list.

Resolve: color emoji prefers a color fallback, then the style face
(bold-italic, else italic, else bold), then primary, then fallbacks.
A miss draws the primary .notdef (glyph id 0).

Printable ASCII (32..126) and U+FFFD at the current pixel size bypass the
LRU. Styled lookups always use the LRU. Changing size drops those slots
and warms ASCII again.
0 when params are unusable.

#### type_place {#type_place}

Source: `Type.h:389`

```c
		    const TypeParams *params);
```

buf must be 16-byte aligned.

#### type_layout_shaped {#type_layout_shaped}

Source: `Type.h:427`

```c
TypeError type_layout_shaped(TypeCtx *ctx, const TypeShapedGlyph *run, uint32_t count,
			     float size_px, TypePositionedGlyph *out, uint32_t cap,
			     uint32_t *written, TypeTextMetrics *metrics);
```

No shaping, bidi, wrapping or fallback is invented here. Use the actual
shaper's glyph order, IDs, clusters and positions. On error, written and
metrics describe the completed prefix; atlas/cache may retain that prefix.
metrics can be requested with out == NULL (cap still bounds the operation).
Glyph advance in out remains nominal; metrics uses shaped advances.

#### type_measure_shaped {#type_measure_shaped}

Source: `Type.h:432`

```c
TypeError type_measure_shaped(const TypeCtx *ctx, const TypeShapedGlyph *run, uint32_t count,
			      float size_px, uint32_t *written, TypeTextMetrics *metrics);
```

Same ink/advance computation without rasterization, scratch, atlas mutation
or cache statistics. count itself is the caller's work bound.

#### type_clear_atlas {#type_clear_atlas}

Clear both atlases and the LRU, then warm ASCII at the last size.

#### type_layout_utf8 {#type_layout_utf8}

Source: `Type.h:442`

```c
TypeError type_layout_utf8(TypeCtx *ctx, const char *text, size_t len, float size_px, TypeCell *out,
			   uint32_t cap, uint32_t *written, size_t *bytes_used);
```

One line at baseline y = 0. x advances by glyph.advance. No wrap, no bidi.
On TYPE_ERR_BUF_TOO_SMALL, *written is cap and *bytes_used is the next
unconsumed byte. On TYPE_ERR_INVALID_UTF8, *bytes_used is the bad byte and
cells before it are kept. Both out-counts may be NULL.
